h1: Cold saws — circular cold saws, manual to CNC carbide
intro: A cold saw cuts metal with a slow-turning, coolant-flooded circular blade instead of a hot abrasive disc, leaving a square, burr-free end that is cool to the touch and ready to weld. Two families of cold saw machines: ISITAN's wet-type circular cold saws for the fabrication shop — the SFC 275 and 315 pull-down saws with a manual or pneumatic vise and the semi-automatic SFC 350-VX with a hydro-pneumatic head — and Bekamak's automatic production saws: the BMDO XS high-speed carbide (TCT) cold saws that cut solid bar to Ø6-1/4″ from a 20 ft magazine loader with servo feeding, and the BMDO CS HSS saws for tube and bar to Ø4″ with a servo gripper feed and touch-screen control. Mitre cuts 45° both ways on the ISITAN saws, blades for mild, high-strength and stainless steel, CSA-approved panels and support from Mississauga, ON.
hero_points: Manual and semi-automatic circular cold saws: round to Ø4-1/2″, mitre 45° both ways, 10-3/4″ – 13-3/4″ HSS blades
Automatic carbide cold saws: solid bar Ø3/8″ – 6-1/4″ at up to 920 ft/min, servo feed, 20 ft magazine loader
Automatic HSS cold saws: tube and bar to Ø4″, ±.004″ feed accuracy, several lengths per bar

faq.q: Cold saw or abrasive chop saw?
faq.a: An abrasive chop saw grinds through the steel at high speed, leaving a hot, burred, slightly bevelled end and sparks. A cold saw cuts with a slow HSS blade (45–90 rpm) under coolant, so the cut is square, cool to the touch, burr-free and ready to weld or fit — and the blade is resharpened dozens of times instead of thrown away.

faq.q: TCT carbide or HSS cold saw?
faq.a: A carbide (TCT) blade runs at 130–920 ft/min and is the fastest way to cut solid steel bar in production — the Bekamak BMDO XS saws are built around it, with servo feeding and a magazine loader for unattended runs. HSS blades run slower (22–130 ft/min on the BMDO CS) and are the choice for tube, thin walls and mixed work; the XS saws accept HSS blades for tube as well.

faq.q: What does an automatic cold saw do by itself?
faq.a: You load bars in the magazine (BMDO XS) or on the roller table (BMDO CS), program the lengths and quantities, and the saw feeds each bar with a servo gripper, clamps it hydraulically, cuts, counts and moves on to the next length — to ±.004″ on the CS and with a 60 mm remnant on the XS.

The SFC V clamps with a hand vise — the simplest saw for occasional cuts. The SFC VP clamps with air at the pull of a lever, which saves time on every cut and holds short pieces better. The SFC 350-VX runs a semi-automatic cycle from a foot switch with a regulated head descent, for batches of the same part without an operator on the handle.

A standard HSS blade cuts mild steel and aluminum. For medium-hard steel we fit TiN-coated blades, TiCN for high-strength steel and TiAlN for stainless. The blade bore is 32 mm with two Ø11 mm pin holes on all SFC models, so blades are readily available in Canada.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
